dialogue.content: こんにちは、相談員です。今日は来てくださりありがとうございます。初めに、年齢と性別を教えていただけますか。
dialogue.English: Hello, I'm the counselor. Thank you for coming in today. To begin, could you please tell me your age and gender?

dialogue.content: こんにちは。よろしくお願いします。26才、女性です。
dialogue.English: Hello. Thank you for seeing me. I'm 26 years old, and female.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。今日は、どのようなご相談でしょうか。
dialogue.English: Thank you. What would you like to talk about today?

dialogue.content: 出産直後で、育児ノイローゼになりそうです
dialogue.English: I've just given birth, and I feel like I’m on the verge of postpartum depression.

dialogue.content: ご出産されて、育児ノイローゼになっておられるのですね。話せる範囲で大丈夫ですので、今どのような状況なのかお話しいただけますか。
dialogue.English: You’ve recently given birth, and it sounds like you may be feeling close to postpartum depression. Please share as much as you feel comfortable—could you tell me what your situation is like right now?

dialogue.content: 出産して退院したあと、実家には戻りませんでした。夫が父親としての自覚を持つようにと。。母がたまに買い物を手伝ってくれています。夫が協力的ではなく、それが1番つらいです。
dialogue.English: After being discharged from the hospital, I didn't return to my parents' home. It was so that my husband would develop a sense of responsibility as a father. My mother sometimes helps with the shopping. The hardest part is that my husband isn't cooperative.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。ご主人様が協力的ではないので、お一人で出産後、体も心も辛いのに、育児に家事をやっていらっしゃって、とても辛いお気持ちなのですね。
dialogue.English: I see. So because your husband isn't being cooperative, you're having to handle all the childcare and housework by yourself, even while you're physically and emotionally exhausted from childbirth. That must be incredibly difficult for you.

dialogue.content: 赤ちゃんは可愛いですが、2、3時間おきに母乳、オムツ替え、消毒、自分の食事や睡眠はいつ取ったのかわからないくらいで。。母が心配するので、夫のことを話せませんが、合コンしたり、スポーツしたり、相変わらず独身者？のようで、自覚がないのです。
dialogue.English: The baby is adorable, but every two or three hours it's breastfeeding, changing diapers, sterilizing things... I can't even remember the last time I ate or slept properly. I can't talk to my mother about my husband because she'd worry, but he's going out to social mixers and playing sports... it's like he's still single. He just doesn't get it.

dialogue.content: 赤ちゃんのお世話は、気持ちの休まることなく、慌ただしくて本当に大変ですよね。お母様にも相談できずに、お一人で、ご主人様のことを考えておられて、とても心が疲弊してしまわれたのですね。
dialogue.English: Taking care of a baby is relentless and truly exhausting, with no time to rest. And since you can't confide in your mother, you've been dealing with your feelings about your husband all alone. You must be completely emotionally exhausted.

dialogue.content: はい、心のうちを話す時間もないし、相手もいない感じです。男の人とこんなに違うものかと。。同じように親になっていくのかと思ったら、夫は育児は女性のすることと、自由にしていて。。
dialogue.English: Yes, I feel like I have neither the time nor anyone to talk to about what's on my mind. I'm shocked at how different men can be... I thought we were becoming parents together, but my husband thinks childcare is a woman’s job and just does as he pleases.

dialogue.content: 共有できないことの落ち込みが激しいです
dialogue.English: I feel deeply discouraged that we can’t share this.

dialogue.content: 一人で辛い思いを抱えておられとても辛かったですね。お話ししてくださり、ありがとうございます。ご主人様に対して、同じ親としてしかりと自覚を持って子育てに参加してほしいきもちなのですね。
dialogue.English: It must have been so difficult for you, holding in all these painful feelings alone. Thank you for opening up to me. It sounds like you want your husband to truly understand his responsibility as a parent and participate in raising your child together.

dialogue.content: はい、そうなんです。でも平日は夜22時過ぎまで帰宅しませんし、週末はスポーツの練習と試合で出かけてしまいます。夜もせっかく寝かせた子を自分のオモチャ代わりのように起こして、自分だけ寝ちゃうんです。
dialogue.English: Yes, exactly. But on weekdays he doesn't get home until after 10 p.m., and on weekends he's out for sports practice and games. At night, after I've finally managed to get the baby to sleep, he'll wake the baby up, treating them like a toy, and then just go to sleep himself.

dialogue.content: まだ自分のことをかまって欲しい子どもみたいな感じ。私の気持ちが赤ちゃんに行って、寂しいのでしょうが、大人になって！と言いたいです。
dialogue.English: He seems like a child who still wants attention for himself. I suppose he feels lonely because my attention is on the baby, but I want to tell him, “Grow up!”

dialogue.content: 平日も休日も、家事に育児にすべてお一人でこなされて、気持ちの面で成長されないご主人に対して怒りの気持ちもわいてきているのですね。
dialogue.English: So you're managing all the housework and childcare by yourself, on both weekdays and weekends, and you're starting to feel angry at your husband for not maturing emotionally.

dialogue.content: はい、私はあなたのお母さんじゃない！って言いたくなります。
dialogue.English: Yes, it makes me want to scream, 'I am not your mother!'

dialogue.content: お子さんの面倒だけでも大変なのに、ご主人の面倒まで見ている状況でしたら、怒りの気持ちがわいてくるのは当然ですよね。一緒に問題解決をしていくために、いくつか質問をさせて頂いてもよろしいでしょうか。
dialogue.English: It's hard enough taking care of a baby, so if you feel like you have to take care of your husband as well, it's completely natural to feel angry. In order to work towards a solution together, would it be okay if I asked you a few questions?

dialogue.content: はい、ありがとうございます
dialogue.English: Yes, thank you.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。今の現状で、ご主人とお話をする時間を作ることは難しいでしょうか。
dialogue.English: Thank you. With the way things are now, would it be difficult to find time to talk with your husband?

dialogue.content: 赤ちゃんが寝ているときはすることが多すぎて、夫は家には寝に帰るだけという感じ。私が何かいうと、また文句？と言います。
dialogue.English: When the baby is sleeping, there's just so much else to do, and it feels like my husband only comes home to sleep. If I try to say something, he just goes, 'Complaining again?'

dialogue.content: そうですよね。赤ちゃんが寝ても、家事が残っていてやることが多いですよね。ご主人も、モモ様の気持ちに寄り添ってお話を聞いてくれる状況ではないのですね。
dialogue.English: I understand. Even when the baby is sleeping, there's still so much housework to do. And it sounds like your husband isn't in a place where he can listen to you with empathy right now.

dialogue.content: 夫は夫で仕事を頑張るし仕事の文句を私に言わないから、私の仕事である育児(彼からすると分業なのでしょう)はそっちでなんとかしてと考えているように思います。彼の親がそうだから。
dialogue.English: My husband works hard and doesn’t complain about his job to me, so I think he believes that childcare—my job, as he sees it in a division of labor—is something I should just handle on my side. That’s how his parents are.

dialogue.content: ご主人も大変な中、お仕事を頑張っているのですね。ご主人のご両親も同じ考えですと、ご主人のご両親には相談できない状況なのですね。今の現状がどのようになれば、モモさんの気持ちが楽になるのでしょうか。
dialogue.English: So your husband is also working very hard. And if his parents share his views, it means you can't really turn to them for advice either. What change in your current situation do you think would bring you some relief?

dialogue.content: 夫の考え方がこうだから、わかって貰おうとしてもダメだろうなとあきらめようとしていました。でも相手への気遣いとかわからないなりに少しは相手の大変さを汲み取ろうして欲しい、少しでもいいので歩み寄りがあると楽になれるかもしれません。
dialogue.English: With his mindset, I was starting to give up, thinking there was no point in trying to get him to understand. But I wish he would at least try to appreciate how difficult this is for me, even if he doesn't fully grasp it. I think I would feel a little better if he could just meet me halfway, even a little.

dialogue.content: なるほど。歩み寄りがあったら、気持ちが楽になるのですね。モモさんはどんな時にもう少し歩み寄ってほしいと思われるのでしょうか。
dialogue.English: I see. So it would bring you some relief if he met you halfway. In what specific situations do you wish he would make more of an effort to do that?

dialogue.content: 大変そうだから、これしておいたよとか行動してくれたらいいのですが。。頼まないと荷物も持ってくれない人なので。。
dialogue.English: It would be nice if he would proactively do something and say, 'You look overwhelmed, so I did this for you.' But he's the kind of person who won't even carry bags unless I specifically ask.

dialogue.content: このまま、あきらめていても、改善はないので、文句と思われないもうな言い方が出来るといいのですが。
dialogue.English: If I just give up, nothing will improve, so I wish I could find a way to communicate that doesn't sound like I'm just complaining.

dialogue.content: ↑思われないないような言い方
dialogue.English: ↑ A way of saying it that doesn't come across as a complaint.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。ご主人は気を利かせて行動することが苦手なのですね。あれやって、なんでやってくれないの。となってしまうと、売り言葉に、買い言葉になってしまい関係がギクシャクしてしまいますよね。Iメッセージというものがあるのですが、あなたが何々をしてくれないといういいかたより、私は何々してほしいと伝えると、案外受け入れてくれることもありますよ。例えば、私はそこの箱をとってもらえると嬉しいなといった感じです。
dialogue.English: I see. So your husband isn't skilled at being proactive. When things become 'Do this' or 'Why didn't you do that?', it can turn into a heated exchange and strain your relationship. There's a communication technique called an 'I-message.' Instead of phrasing things as 'You didn't do something,' you express it as 'I would like...' He may be more receptive to that. For example, 'I would be so happy if you could get that box for me.'

dialogue.content: そうですね、ついついなんでしてくれないの？という気持ちがそのままことばになりますから、気をつけてみます
dialogue.English: You're right. The feeling of 'Why won't you do it?' tends to come straight out of my mouth, so I will try to be more mindful.

dialogue.content: 赤ちゃんを育てながら、夫育ても。。気が重いですが、やってみます。
dialogue.English: Raising a baby while also trying to 'raise' my husband... It feels overwhelming, but I'll give it a try.

dialogue.content: 子育てをしながらでは、余裕がないですよね。でも頑張って改善していこうとする、前向きなモモさんの姿がとても素敵です。無理のない範囲でやってみて、またお話しをしにきてくださると嬉しいです。今日はありがとうございました。また、お待ちしていますね。
dialogue.English: You certainly don't have much extra capacity while raising a child. But it's wonderful that you have such a positive attitude and are willing to work on improving the situation. Please just try what you can without overdoing it, and I would be happy if you came back to talk again. Thank you for your time today. I look forward to our next session.

dialogue.content: はい、誰かにこの気持ちを聞いて頂けたこと、とてもありがたかったです。
dialogue.English: Yes, I’m very grateful to have had someone listen to how I feel.

dialogue.content: では赤ちゃんが泣いていますので、失礼さます。ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: The baby is crying now, so I have to go. Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: こちらこそ、お話しして下さり、ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Thank you as well, for sharing your story with me.

dialogue.content: (ではこれで失礼しますね、ありがとうございました。評価入れさせて頂きます)
dialogue.English: (Okay, I'll end the session here. Thank you. I will submit my evaluation.)

dialogue.content: モモさんありがとうございました。これでロールプレー終了ボタン押しますね。
dialogue.English: Thank you, Momo. I'm pressing the end role-play button now.
